A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same stochastic multiscale modeling work. Their complete main texts and appendices provide readable equations, tables, figures, and experimental details sufficient to match content across the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original trained-model results for KdV, Burgers, and cylinder flow, including error statistics, microscale-dimension ablations, and appendix diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 reports original results across five systems, including Burgers in Appendix H.3, with baseline comparisons, ablations, and computational-cost analysis.

M1.justification: The coupled SDEs, PoE likelihood, and hierarchical variational training remain. However, v2 changes ReLU to LeakyReLU, revises convolutional architectures, and replaces cylinder flow's learned space/time coupling network with identity coupling and spatial Fourier features (v1 Appendix G.4; v2 Appendix H.6). These are architectural adaptations within the retained framework.

E1.justification: v2 adds one-dimensional wave advection and two-dimensional shallow-water radial dam-break evaluation, substantially broadening the represented dynamics and initial-condition families. KdV and cylinder flow remain; Burgers is retained in Appendix H.3 rather than removed.

E2.justification: v1's predictive comparisons use the implicit-scale baseline. v2 adds coarse DNS, DMD, and POD-SINDy to the retained KdV, Burgers, and cylinder experiments, as verified in Tables 1 and 3. Full DNS also supplies a computational-cost reference in Figure 8.

E3.justification: v2 introduces baseline dimension matching and validation-based POD-SINDy tuning, alongside protocols for the added tasks. Existing training settings also change: batch size and quadrature count decrease from 128 to 64, KdV training from 200 to 100 epochs, and cylinder training from 2000 to 1000 epochs (v1 Appendix G.5; v2 Appendix H.7).

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantive accuracy-versus-inference-cost study across four systems using NFE times state dimension (Figure 8), addressing efficiency beyond v1's accuracy ablations. Microscale-dimension and spatial diagnostics extend to the added systems. Existing drift-sensitivity and kernel-spectrum analyses remain, while the two-dimensional implicit-scale error/uncertainty comparisons are removed.

E5.justification: Test-set mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and predictive covariance estimation remain. However, v1's implicit-scale predictive-standard-deviation maps in Figures 11 and 17–18 disappear; v2 Figures 20–22 retain only the multiscale uncertainty maps. Neither version reports a repeated-training-run or seed-based significance protocol.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, wave, shallow-water, and cost results. Retained-case values change in both directions: KdV mean error at n_eta=1 changes from 0.103 to 0.197, while cylinder error at n_eta=5 changes from 0.031 to 0.009 (Table 1). Revised architectures and training settings prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3 states an unweighted reconstruction mean that conflicts with its precision-weighted PoE expression in Section 4.4 and Appendix F. v2 removes that inconsistent equality and explicitly displays the weighted mean in Equation 9. The PoE, ELBO, predictive-moment, and memory-kernel derivations otherwise remain substantively equivalent.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain stochastic scale-separated dynamics, the PoE likelihood, and simulator-free learning. v2 extends the abstract, introduction, and conclusion's comparative claims to reduced-order modeling, explicitly claiming superiority over DMD and POD-SINDy, particularly for slowly decaying Kolmogorov n-width.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for DMD's competitiveness on periodic cylinder flow and ROM difficulties on shallow water, plus specific limitations concerning local structures in three-dimensional turbulence and long-term chaotic stability. v1's excluded unstable Burgers trajectory and proposed stability-preserving remedy are no longer discussed; v2 does not establish whether that failure was resolved.

D1.justification: New Appendix G documents baseline implementations, cubic interpolation, POD-SINDy tuning and selected hyperparameters, and DMD regularization. v2 also supplies added-task preprocessing, revised architecture/training specifications, and cumulative training-time formulas. This substantially expands reproducibility information; the underlying code-repository location remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially expands positioning against global ROM, neural SDE closures requiring solver-based training, and hierarchical graph weather models. New references include Parish and Duraisamy, Gupta and Lermusiaux, Lam et al., and Oskarsson et al. These substantive comparisons go beyond the retained ROM/Mori–Zwanzig overview and bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the method exposition, related work, experimental narrative, and conclusion, and standardizes encoder/decoder terminology. It moves Burgers into Appendix H.3, adds a dedicated baseline appendix, and reorganizes architecture descriptions and supplementary plots into clearer subsections.

P2.justification: Tables are restructured for expanded benchmarks and comparators, baseline prediction panels are enlarged, and a cost figure and supplementary-figure index are added. Many rotated full-page appendix plots are regrouped into upright multipanel layouts. These are substantial display changes beyond updated numerical entries.

improvement.justification: v1's broad predictive claims relied mainly on an internal implicit-scale comparison. v2 substantially strengthens their evaluation through coarse-DNS, DMD, and tuned POD-SINDy comparisons, two additional physical systems, and detailed baseline protocols (Tables 1 and 3; Appendix G). The cost-proxy study also addresses efficiency directly. Reduced comparative uncertainty reporting and the unexplained disappearance of the Burgers failure disclosure weaken transparency, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support and reproducibility.
